title: Reuters: Entities Behind Trump's $TRUMP Coin Made Up to $100 Million in Trading Fees
description_short: Reuters reported that entities behind Trump's $TRUMP coin accumulated an estimated $86M–$100M in trading fees by Jan. 30, less than two weeks after its Jan. 17 launch.
description_medium: Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP memecoin on Jan. 17, 2025. Reuters cited estimates from three blockchain analysis firms that the token generated $86 million to $100 million in trading fees by Jan. 30, less than two weeks later. The estimate concerns fees accumulated by entities behind the coin, not a documented $100 million payment by foreign buyers.
description_long: Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP memecoin on Jan. 17, 2025, three days before his inauguration. Reuters reported that the token quickly surged, reaching a market capitalization above $14.5 billion on Jan. 19. In a Feb. 3 report, Reuters cited estimates from three blockchain analysis firms that the token generated between $86 million and $100 million in trading fees by Jan. 30, less than two weeks after launch. Reuters described those fees as accumulated by entities behind the coin. This reported fee total is distinct from the frozen description’s claim that the initial trading surge “raised over $100 million”: the source estimates trading fees over the following period, not a $100 million launch-day raise. It also does not establish that anonymous wallet owners were foreign, document a hidden payment channel, or report that the SEC declined to investigate. The revised entry therefore retains the launch and fee story while removing unsupported claims about buyer nationality, foreign payments, and an SEC decision.

source_fact_map.fact: Reuters reported that Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP memecoin on Jan. 17, 2025, and that it quickly surged to a peak market value above $14.5 billion by Jan. 19.
source_fact_map.quote: The meme coin, known as $Trump, was launched by the president on Jan. 17 and quickly surged, reaching a peak of over $14.5 billion in overall market value by Jan. 19, the day before his inauguration.
limitations: This does not establish wallet owners’ nationalities or the source of individual buyers’ funds.

source_fact_map.fact: Reuters reported estimates from three blockchain analysis firms that the token generated between $86 million and $100 million in trading fees by Jan. 30.
source_fact_map.quote: Three crypto data firms, including Merkle Science and Chainalysis, analyzed the blockchain, a publicly available ledger that shows all transactions involving $Trump, for Reuters. They estimated that the $Trump token had generated between $86 million and $100 million in trading fees by Jan. 30.
limitations: The estimate concerns trading fees over the period after launch, not $100 million raised in the initial trading surge.

source_fact_map.fact: Reuters described entities behind the coin as accumulating close to $100 million in trading fees in less than two weeks, based on estimates from three blockchain analysis firms.
source_fact_map.quote: Entities behind President Donald Trump’s crypto coin have accumulated close to $100 million in trading fees in less than two weeks, according to estimates from three blockchain analysis firms, a large windfall from a venture that has seen tens of thousands of small traders lose money.
limitations: The excerpt does not identify foreign wallet owners, describe an undisclosed payment channel, or report an SEC decision not to investigate.

frozen_original.title: Trump $TRUMP Memecoin Raises $100M+ from Anonymous Foreign Wallets
frozen_original.synopsis: Days before his second inauguration, Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP memecoin, a cryptocurrency bearing his image and brand. The token raised over $100 million in its initial trading surge, with blockchain analysts identifying a significant share of purchases coming from anonymous wallets suspected of foreign origins. The launch gave foreign actors a mechanism to transfer funds to Trump-affiliated entities without disclosure, effectively creating an untraceable foreign payment channel. The Securities and Exchange Commission under Trump's own appointees declined to investigate. Critics called it the most blatant foreign influence operation since the invention of modern campaign finance law.

staged_snapshot.title: Reuters: $TRUMP Buyers Spent an Estimated $148 Million to Qualify for a Dinner
staged_snapshot.description_short: Reuters estimated buyers spent $148 million on $TRUMP tokens to qualify for a May 2025 dinner with Trump; the amount was based on token holdings, not a proven direct payment.
staged_snapshot.description_medium: Reuters reported that 220 top holders of the $TRUMP memecoin attended a May 22, 2025, dinner at Trump’s private club. It estimated their qualifying holdings at $148 million, including more than $111 million among the top 25, citing Inca Digital. Blockchain analysis suggested more than half of attendees were likely outside the United States; wallet data did not establish their nationalities.

The supplied synopsis also claims an undisclosed payment channel and an SEC decision not to investigate without supporting passages.
Proposed correction: Distinguish the initial token launch from the later investor dinner, and avoid labeling wallet owners foreign or describing an SEC decision until those claims are sourced.

Source check: Reuters’ supplied May 22, 2025 URL returned HTTP 401 (“HTTP Forbidden”), so its article text and named investors could not be read. The URL identifies a later $TRUMP dinner story, not January 2025 launch transactions. It supplies no directly verified launch-period trading total, wallet-owner nationality, payment channel, or SEC decision; those claims remain unsupported by the accessible linked material.

rationale: A focused Reuters source search found contemporaneous reporting that Trump launched $TRUMP on Jan. 17 and reporting that estimates $86–100 million in trading fees had accumulated by Jan. 30. The proposal corrects the frozen “raised over $100 million in its initial trading surge” claim to a fee estimate spanning less than two weeks; it removes the unsupported foreign-wallet nationality, undisclosed payment-channel, and SEC non-investigation assertions. The prior held204 record remains a hold and is not treated as approval. The May dinner URLs remain research history only.
